# nx_burst: simulated time to detection per DGA family

**This is a simulation, not field data.** Generated by `agents/dga_eval/nx_sim.py`: one infected device looks up its family's names from the Netlab 360 DGA feed (chrmor/DGA_domains_dataset, pinned by hash, 25 families) in feed order, one name every GAP seconds, through the real `Resolver.decide()` in shadow mode with the shipped models and the default config (`nx_burst_min_distinct` 10, `nx_burst_window` 600 s, `recommend_threshold` 0.96, `burst_min_score` 0.8). Scorer backend: trm+lr.

Assumptions: every looked-up name is unregistered and answers NXDOMAIN (with the TLD's SOA). The query gap is a parameter, not a measured property of each family. The device does nothing else. There is no real home traffic in this repository, so this says nothing about false positives on real networks; the guards against those are unit-tested (`agents/ghost_dns/tests/test_nx_burst.py`).

Cells are `lookups until the first alert (minutes)`; `no` = not within 300 lookups.

nx_burst fired for 25/25 families at 1 lookup / 2 s, 25/25 families at 1 lookup / 10 s, 25/25 families at 1 lookup / 30 s, 25/25 families at 1 lookup / 60 s. "model: single-name alert" is the share of 2000 sampled names scoring >= 0.96 (`dga_suspect`/`dga_high`); "counts toward dga_burst" is the share scoring >= 0.8. Slower than one lookup per 67 s, 10 names never fit in one 600 s window. One storm raises one alert: where dga_burst alerts first, nx_burst's detector still fires at the lookup shown but its alert is skipped.
